resources.string: Peer relays are devices of your tailnet that carry traffic for two devices that cannot connect directly, usually faster than Tailscale\'s DERP servers. A rule here says which devices may use which relays. The relay itself is switched on on the device, tailscale set --relay-server-port=40000, with that UDP port reachable. Both sides need Tailscale 1.86 or newer; Android, iOS and Apple TV cannot relay.
Pick a rule to see and change it
No peer relays yet: devices that cannot connect directly go through Tailscale\'s DERP servers
%1$s: shared from another tailnet, and relays serve only their own
Its devices are those of the access it gives, so they are changed on the Access page. Make the relays a rule of their own to edit them here.
Make a rule of its own
The devices that relay, by tag, host, IP set or Tailscale address. Each relays only once it is switched on there: tailscale set --relay-server-port=40000.
Devices that stay in one place behind a strict NAT or firewall, in an office or a cloud network. Not phones and laptops that change networks, and not everyone: each of them would try the relays.
From the console\'s device list. It tells what a device runs, not whether its relay is switched on: that is set on the device and shown there by tailscale status.
Which devices relay, and for whom
Choose the relays and the devices that may use them first.
Every device of this kind would try the relays, and its traffic could take a longer way. Tailscale advises naming the devices behind a strict NAT instead.
